review: 1:1 טוֹב שׁוֹמֵר — 'the best of watchers', for نِعْمَ الرَّقِيب; the Arabic nعْمَ construction has no Hebrew equivalent, so the superlative adjective carries it.
1:3 אֵל שַׁדַּי — the patriarchal divine name is used for الْقَدِير ('the Almighty'), which is its standard rendering.
2:1–2:2 — the Arabic pairs 'wastes and deserts' with 'where thirst is'; Hebrew sets מִדְבָּר against שְׁמָמָה and keeps צָמָא, the word of Isa 35:7, where the thirsty ground becomes springs.
3:2 סוֹבֵב מַעֲלוֹתַיִךְ — 'enfolds your goings'; מַעֲלוֹת is used for the steps of a journey (Ps 121:3's 'going out'), matching مَسِيرَكِ.
4:1 מְחוֹז חֶפְצֵךְ — 'the haven of your desire', for مَقْصِدُكِ; מָחוֹז is the biblical 'haven' (Ps 107:30), which keeps the sea-voyage image behind the hymn.
